origin.description: Read the stored bytes of a string in a chosen encoding and return UTF-8 text.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector. Bytes created with rawToChar keep the encoding mark unknown, so the converter reads those bytes.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.text: One encoding name, such as a name from stringi::stri_enc_list.

origin.details: encoding must be a single string. NULL becomes one missing string, not an empty vector. An unknown encoding name is an ICU file-access error. Names on string are copied.
origin.value: A character vector of UTF-8 strings the same length as string, except that NULL has length 1 and is missing.
origin.example:
x <- rawToChar(as.raw(177))
cat(paste0("str_conv(x, \"ISO-8859-2\") returns ", str_conv(x, "ISO-8859-2"), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_conv(x, \"ISO-8859-1\") returns ", str_conv(x, "ISO-8859-1"), ".\n"))

translation.description: Reinterpret bytes with stringi.stri_conv and request UTF-8.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, bytes, or a list of those. bytes stands for an unknown-encoding R string. None is one missing result.

translation.details: A bytes value is decoded in encoding and encoded as UTF-8. A Python string is read as its UTF-8 bytes. An unknown name raises the ICU file-access error. The result is a list, and names on a character vector are copied.
translation.value: A list of UTF-8 strings. NULL is a list of one NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.escape import str_conv
x = bytes([177])
print("str_conv(x, \"ISO-8859-2\") returns " + str_conv(x, "ISO-8859-2")[0] + ".")
print("str_conv(x, \"ISO-8859-1\") returns " + str_conv(x, "ISO-8859-1")[0] + ".")
